## Part 1: Vectorizing code 

```{r}
# Question 1.a
fun1 <- function(n = 100, k = 4, lambda = 4) {
  x <- NULL
  
  for (i in 1:n)
    x <- rbind(x, rpois(k, lambda))
  
  return(x)
}

# rbind will use a lot more memory than we need, so we have to prespecify its dimension
fun1alt <- function(n = 100, k = 4, lambda = 4) {
  x <- matrix(NA, nrow = n, ncol = k)
  for (i in 1:n)
    x[i,] <- rpois(k, lambda)
  return(x)
}

# Benchmarking
bench::mark(
  fun1(),
  fun1alt(), relative = TRUE, check = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
# Total row sums
fun1 <- function(mat) {
  n <- nrow(mat)
  ans <- double(n) 
  for (i in 1:n) {
    ans[i] <- sum(mat[i, ])
  }
  ans
}

# we are doing row sum of matrix, and there is a function that can do it
fun1alt <- function(mat) {
  ans <- rowSums(mat)
  ans
}

# Cumulative sum by row
fun2 <- function(mat) {
  n <- nrow(mat)
  k <- ncol(mat)
  ans <- mat
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 2:k) { # for each row
      ans[i,j] <- mat[i, j] + ans[i, j - 1] #cum sum of all previous cells of this row
    }
  }
  ans
}

# I know cumsum works on list
# so I have to apply this to each row of matrix
fun2alt <- function(mat) {
  t(apply(mat, 1, cumsum))
}

# Use the data with this code
set.seed(2315)
dat <- matrix(rnorm(200 * 100), nrow = 200)

# Test for the first
bench::mark(
  fun1(dat),
  fun1alt(dat), relative = TRUE
)

# Test for the second
bench::mark(
  fun2(dat),
  fun2alt(dat), relative = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# Data Generating Process (10 x 10,000 matrix)
set.seed(1234)
x <- matrix(rnorm(1e4), nrow=10)

# Find each column's max value
fun2 <- function(x) {
  apply(x, 2, max)
}

# following the hint, we found that max.col() can only find the max value of each row, but here we want to know that of columns
# need to use t()
fun2alt <- function(x) {
  index <- max.col(t(x)) # index of max value of each column of x(which is row number)
  x[cbind(index, seq_len(ncol(x)))]
}

# Benchmarking
bench::mark(
  fun2(x),
  fun2alt(x), relative = TRUE
)
```

# Part 2: Rcpp

```{r}
Rcpp::sourceCpp("scale_free.cpp")

set.seed(3312)
g <- scale_free(n = 500, m = 2)
```

```{r}
## Visualizing the degree distribution
library(ggplot2)
data.frame(degree = colSums(g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(degree)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Degree\n(log10 scale)",
    y = "Count"
  )
```
